title: Back then, editing was eating 30 hours of my week.
caption:
Back then, editing was eating 30 hours of my week.

Cutting every pause. Timing every caption. Zooming in, by hand. So I stopped editing: now I film one take and tell Claude what I want in plain English.

It times every word, cuts the dead air, checks that no words were lost and punches in on the hook. Then it shows me a plan and waits for my OK before it renders. Now filming and editing take me under an hour a day.

10 Things You Didn't Know Claude Could Do · #8. Up next, #7: could Claude run a channel without me on camera?

What eats the most time in your edits: cutting pauses, timing captions or adding zooms?

title: In 2010, a computer worm was caught going after Iran's nuclear program.
caption:
In 2010, a computer worm was caught going after Iran's nuclear program.

At Natanz, thousands of centrifuges spun underground, run by computers cut off from the internet. So the worm most likely rode in on a USB drive, using four unpatched Windows flaws at once.

Then it waited for one exact setup. When it found it, it pushed the motors up to 1,410 hertz, dragged them down toward two, then brought them back, and hid it from the people watching the controls.

In 2012, The New York Times reported it was an American and Israeli operation. Neither country has openly admitted it.

Next in Kill Switch, Part 4: the next big breach started with something much smaller, a password stolen from a heating and cooling contractor.

Would your workplace notice if a USB drive did this?

#KillSwitch #Stuxnet #CyberSecurity #TechHistory #Hacking

title: In 1990, Robert Tappan Morris became the first person ever convicted of computer fraud in America. Here's how it happene
caption:
In 1990, Robert Tappan Morris became the first person ever convicted of computer fraud in America. Here's how it happened.

It's November 2, 1988, and the internet is just a few universities, labs and military sites. A 22 year old Cornell grad student has written a program that spreads all by itself. To cover his tracks, he releases it from MIT's network.

But there's a bug. Even when a computer says it's already infected, the worm copies itself anyway, one time out of seven. The copies pile up and computers slow to a crawl. The usual estimate is around 6,000 machines.

This is Part 1 of Kill Switch, where we talk about the hacks that changed history. Up next in Part 2: he never meant any harm, but the next one wanted to be loved. Its subject line was just three words: I LOVE YOU.

He got three years probation and 400 hours of community service. Too light, too heavy, or about right?

#KillSwitch #MorrisWorm #CyberSecurity #TechHistory #Hacking

title: Three words. I love you. That's all it took to infect tens of millions of computers in 2000.
caption:
Three words. I love you. That's all it took to infect tens of millions of computers in 2000.

May 4, 2000. An email spreads out of the Philippines with a love letter attached. It looks like a harmless text file, but Windows is hiding the end of its name. It's really a script.

Open it, and it mails itself to everyone in your address book. Britain's House of Commons shuts its servers down for two hours. Later estimates put the damage at around $10 billion.

Watch the full episode 👉🏾 https://www.facebook.com/reel/1511967917426987/

Part 3: ten years later, someone built a real weapon and aimed it at a nuclear plant.

Would you have opened that love letter?

title: Besides the amazing times with friends and discusssing business was hands down the “Pen Game”
caption:
Besides the amazing times with friends and discusssing business was hands down the “Pen Game”

Everyone starts with the same item and you spend a set time (1 hour when we did it because I had a flight to catch) and you see what you can trade up too without spending any money or telling anyone you’re playing a game. It was challenging but as the game progresses and post recap it’s all about perception economics. Plenty of people will give you things for free just because but you’ve gotta understand what it is they want and the many many things we can use outside of money to exchange value. I did see a guy rob target in the midst of it and sell tvs for $30-$100 and even though Target says it’s $300 to that guy possibly getting sent to jail and $30 was worth that 32 inch…it’s not always that extreme but it’s definitely worth thinking about 🤔
